trend-analysis.name: Trend Analysis
trend-analysis.summary: Identify and discuss data-driven patterns to understand performance and forecast what's next. Useful for market reviews, strategic outlooks, and any deck where the audience must act on a direction-of-travel call.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open by establishing why this trend matters now. Tie it to a decision on the table or a forecast that's about to be made. Trends without consequences are filler.

beats.name: Historical Comparison
beats.description: Contrast current data with the relevant past. Pick the comparison window that makes the trend visible without cherry-picking. Be honest about base effects.

beats.name: Pattern Identification
beats.description: Name the recurring outcome you've spotted. Use one or two strong charts that show the pattern unambiguously. Avoid overclaiming significance from a small N.

beats.name: Future Prediction
beats.description: Project where the trend leads if it continues. Show the forecast and the confidence interval. State the assumptions that would have to break for the prediction to fail.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: Translate the prediction into the strategy it implies. Specific actions, sequenced. Each action should map to a particular reading of the trend, not a generic best practice.

beats.name: Implementation
beats.description: Walk through how the actions get executed: owners, milestones, monitoring. The audience should leave understanding what to do tomorrow, not just what to think about.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Recap the trend, the forecast, and the recommended action. End with the leading indicator you'll watch to know if the call is right.

marketing.name: Marketing
marketing.summary: Marketing professionals analyzing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategies.
marketing.description: Marketing professionals reviewing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategy. Make the funnel visible, highlight engagement metrics, keep the brand consistent, and tell the story visually. Moderate chart density; 15-30 slides.

sales.name: Sales
sales.summary: Sales team or prospective customers focused on product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI justification.
sales.description: Sales teams and prospective customers weighing product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI. Put customer success stories first, back claims with visual proof points, state the value proposition plainly, and close on a strong call to action. Moderate chart density; 15-25 slides.

plan.name: Plan
plan.summary: Establish a roadmap, operating plan, or sequence of actions with owners and next steps.
plan.description: Use when the deck should turn strategy into coordinated action. Make sequencing, ownership, dependencies, risks, and checkpoints visible.
plan.outcome: The audience understands the plan and accepts the next actions.

authoritative.name: Authoritative
authoritative.summary: Expert, declarative voice for category-defining and analyst-style decks.
authoritative.description: Adopt the perspective of someone who's seen the full landscape and is willing to call it. Use plain declaratives — strong claims with the receipts to back them. Step back from internal-only context and frame in terms the wider industry would recognize.
voiceCues: Use declarative sentences; trust the reader to follow.
Frame in industry-wide terms, not company-internal language.
Cite outside sources — analysts, benchmarks, public peers.
Take a position; avoid 'on the other hand' symmetry without a verdict.
avoid: Hedging ('we believe', 'in our view') unless deliberately contrasting.
First-person plural overload — speak for the work, not the team.
Tentative phrasing that softens strong claims.
samplePhrases: Agent latency is the bottleneck of the next AI cycle.
Three categories will absorb 80% of enterprise budget; we're built for the second.
The benchmarks are public; the gap holds across every comparable workload.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

black-and-white.summary: Strict monochrome contrast for formal, document-style decks.
black-and-white.description: A pure black-and-white scheme for decks that need maximum restraint, print compatibility, and crisp information hierarchy.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

montserrat.name: Montserrat
montserrat.description: Montserrat is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Montserrat for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
